messages:
Alex: quick sync — API is leaning toward a soft-queue + immediate 429 for per-key sustained-limit breaches, and falling back to 503 only when node-level memory/cpu is exhausted. want opinions before we lock config on dedicated.
Maria: can you sketch the flow? soft-queue meaning a short-lived in-memory queue on the edge, or a routed queue in the frontend dispatcher?
Alex: short-lived in-memory at the edge (~250ms target), otherwise route to per-org backlog queue with token-bucket admission. idea is to avoid upstream 503 cascades while keeping latency SLOs.
Kevin: i like avoiding 503 for most client errors. question: how do we choose 429 vs delayed accept + queue? if it's per-key burst we want to accept bursts, but per-org sustained should be throttled earlier.
Liz: from SRE POV 503 should be reserved for system-level backpressure. 429 should indicate client-level quota. mixing them confuses downstream retries. also need clear headers so clients can distinguish "quota_exceeded" vs "service_unavailable".
Jordan: +1 on header visibility. For console UX we should also surface the reason (per-key vs per-org vs system) in the request breakdown and on the quota page.
Maria: we need a small config shape. proposal:

```
# limiter config (proposal)
per_key: {sustained_rps: 10, burst_tokens: 100, burst_window_ms: 1000}
per_org: {sustained_rps: 200, burst_tokens: 500, burst_window_ms: 2000}
system: {max_inflight: 20000, queue_capacity: 5000}
```

Maria: enforcement rules:
- if key exceeds burst_tokens but system healthy => accept and mark as "burst" (emit metric)
- if key exceeds sustained_rps consistently => 429 with Retry-After and quota headers
- if system inflight > max_inflight OR memory pressure high => reject route with 503 and X-Redwood-Overloaded: true

Kevin: how do we avoid thundering herd on fallback queues? if many keys get redirected to per-org backlog, that queue could blow up.
Alex: plan is to have per-org backlog use a priority window (recent successful requests get higher priority) and a jittered re-enqueue. also cap requeue attempts per request id.
Liz: we should also prefer shedding low-cost requests? or cheaper tokens first? cost vs latency tradeoffs.
Jordan: product note — we should provide a toggle in the console: "prefer latency (deny bursts)" vs "prefer throughput (allow bursts)" per org.
Maria: telemetry: emit these metrics per request: limiter_decision={allow|burst|queue|reject_system|reject_quota}, queue_latency_ms, quota_type={per_key|per_org|system}, dropped=true/false
ops-bot: Incidentbot: if system queue > 80% capacity for 5m, create paging alert to SRE with summary + top offending orgs.
Kevin: for retries, clients should backoff on 503 aggressively and don't retry 429 until Retry-After. we should document client guidance in SDKs.
Alex: devops: who owns the rollout? want a staged toggle: default to current behavior for 10% of traffic, log both codes for 48h, then flip.
Liz: rollout plan sounds safe. add a canary metric: proportion of 503s that would have been 429 under new rules.
Maria: okay i'll draft PR for limiter with config + headers + telemetry and add console toggle. will include sample SDK guidance and doc snippet.
Jordan: please include console wireframe showing per-org slider for "burst allowance".
Alex: thanks all — will post PR link when ready. :thumbsup
